name: Lower eyelid retraction surgery

card.summary: A family of eyelid procedures, including spacer grafts, canthal suspension and midface lifting, that raise a low or retracted lower lid to reduce scleral show and give the eye a more almond-shaped look.
card.aka: Lower lid retraction repair; almond eye surgery; lower eyelid lengthening
card.note: Surgical outcomes can be unpredictable and revision surgery is described as difficult; complications can affect comfort and vision.

quick.overview:
Lower eyelid retraction means the lower lid margin sits below its normal position, showing white sclera under the iris and sometimes giving a round, sad or staring look. Surgeons treat it with a set of procedures that lift and support the lower lid, and in looksmaxxing forums the aesthetic version is often called almond eye surgery.

The appearance payoff people describe is less scleral show and a more almond-shaped, tilted eye. The published literature is largely about repairing retraction after blepharoplasty or from thyroid eye disease, so it describes techniques and outcomes in those patients, with a handful of randomized trials comparing graft materials.
quick.how: The surgery is done by oculoplastic or facial plastic surgeons and typically combines elements such as a spacer graft in the back layer of the lid (cartilage, hard-palate mucosa or acellular dermal matrix), release of scar in the middle layer, midface lifting and canthal suspension at the outer corner. Which elements are used depends on the cause and which layers of the lid are deficient.
quick.risks: Reviews describe surgical correction as difficult and unpredictable, and patient dissatisfaction is a recognised issue, so counselling about expectations is stressed. Retraction itself can cause dry eye, irritation and exposure of the cornea. Community threads discuss botched cases and long waits and high costs with leading surgeons.

lead: Lower eyelid retraction is a malposition in which the lower eyelid margin sits abnormally low, exposing white sclera between the lid and the iris and widening the eye opening. Lower eyelid retraction surgery is the family of procedures used to raise and support the lid. Its most common medical causes are thyroid eye disease and complications of lower eyelid cosmetic surgery, and it can also be congenital or follow trauma, strabismus surgery or facial nerve palsy.[1][2][25][26]

The appearance payoff people describe is a lower lid line that sits closer to the lower edge of the iris, which reduces scleral show and can make the eye read as less round, less "sad" or staring, and more almond-shaped. In looksmaxxing communities the aesthetic version is known as almond eye surgery. Forum users discuss it alongside canthoplasty, fat grafting, fillers and orbital implants, and compare surgeons, consultation fees and waiting times.[3][4][28][29]

Clinical research on the topic is mostly reviews, technique descriptions and retrospective series, plus a limited number of randomized trials comparing graft materials. A retrospective Korean series found that surgery corrected congenital and acquired retraction in all treated eyelids, and surgeons describe an escalating ladder of options from lateral canthal tightening to spacer grafts and midface lifting depending on severity and which layers of the lid are deficient.[5][24][25]

chain: Spacer graft, scar release and canthal support lift the lower lid
Less scleral show beneath the iris
Eye reads as more almond-shaped with a firmer lower lid line
angle.text: The procedures raise the lower lid margin and support the outer corner, which reduces visible sclera under the iris and changes the eye's outline. Forum users pursuing almond eye surgery describe this as improving canthal tilt and the look of the eye area.

paras: Lower eyelid retraction is defined as downward malposition of the lower eyelid margin without the lid turning outward, and it presents with scleral show, round or sad-looking eyes, laxity of the lateral canthal tendon and symptoms such as irritation, tearing and incomplete closure during sleep.[10] The University of Iowa EyeRounds tutorial defines it as inferior displacement of the lid exposing sclera below the limbus, without eversion or inversion.[25]

It may involve deficiency of one or more of the lid's three layers: the skin and muscle (anterior lamella), the middle layer of septum and retractors, and the back layer of tarsus and conjunctiva (posterior lamella).[1][25] Surgeons often describe three patterns: involutional retraction from horizontal laxity, cicatricial retraction from scarring of the middle layer, and retraction related to prominent (proptotic) eyes.[26]

Diagnosis is clinical. Lid position is compared with the lower edge of the cornea, often using margin reflex distance 2 (MRD2). Descriptions vary on the threshold, with values above about 5 mm, 5.5 mm or 6 mm used.[1][24][25] Examination also assesses lid laxity with a distraction test, orbicularis tone with a snap test, and tear film and corneal exposure.[26]

A review of post-blepharoplasty retraction describes the standard surgery as combining midface lifting, a posterior lamellar spacer graft and canthal suspension, and reports variable degrees of functional and aesthetic improvement.[2] Canthal suspension procedures, which tighten or reposition the outer corner, are described as an adjunct to lower lid surgery and include open and closed suspension and canthopexy.[6]

Spacer grafts have been made from autologous ear cartilage, hard-palate mucosa, acellular dermal matrix such as AlloDerm, and porous polyethylene (Medpor), and reviews compare graft contraction with each.[7][8][9][11] The EyeRounds tutorial classes spacers as epithelial-lined (upper lid tarsoconjunctiva, hard palate, nasal mucosa) or non-epithelial-lined (dermis fat, auricular cartilage, processed dermal products), and says they vertically lengthen the middle or posterior lamella.[25]

In thyroid eye disease, retractor release and recession of the inferior rectus have been described, and hyaluronic acid gel has been reported as a temporary expansion option.[12][13][14] Transconjunctival lower blepharoplasty is discussed as a way to reduce the risk of causing retraction in the first place.[15]

The EyeRounds tutorial describes a "finger test" used in planning: if a finger at the outer corner is enough to reposition the lid, a lateral tarsal strip or canthopexy is considered; if more of the lid and cheek must be moved to restore position, anterior or mucosal spacers, malar fat pad elevation and subperiosteal midface elevation are added.[25] Skin shortage alone is treated with skin grafting, and limited shortage with a midface lift with or without a graft.[25]

A 2017 retrospective series from a Korean eye hospital reviewed 19 lower eyelids in 14 patients aged 12 to 57 who were treated between 2006 and 2013. Causes were congenital retraction in 7 eyelids (treated for cosmetic reasons), prior strabismus, blepharoplasty, orbital fracture or lacrimal surgery in most of the rest, plus facial palsy and one unexplained case.[24] Mild cases (under 2 mm asymmetry and MRD2 under 6.5 mm) were treated with lateral canthal tightening without grafts, while 13 eyelids received an acellular dermal allograft spacer through the conjunctival side.[24] Mean MRD2 fell from 7.49 mm to 5.65 mm at one month, the authors reported correction in all eyelids with no complications, and they noted the retrospective design and small size as limits.[24]

A narrative review in Seminars in Plastic Surgery summarises the broader literature, including a 199-patient series of vertical midface lifts in which 98 percent showed objective improvement and a 342-case series of concentric malar lifts reporting functional and aesthetic gains. It describes most of the evidence as retrospective series and small comparisons.[23]

Hyaluronic acid filler is described as a temporary option for mild retraction or for people with corneal exposure.[14][26] Fat grafting, infraorbital rim and cheek implants, orbital decompression and lateral canthoplasty are discussed as other routes to eye-area support. A plastic surgeon writing about congenital inferior scleral show describes it as a tissue deficiency at several levels and says canthoplasty alone is best viewed as an adjunct rather than a standalone fix; he favours adding infraorbital rim support and a spacer graft. This is one practitioner's published opinion rather than a trial result.[27]

The Review of Ophthalmology summary stresses that in thyroid eye disease surgery is generally delayed until the disease is inactive, and that a temporary traction suture is commonly used after surgery to hold the lower lid up while it heals.[26]

Forum users compile lists of surgeons, consultation fees and waiting times, and discuss near-term plans, healing updates and before-and-after cases. One looksmax.org thread ranking US surgeons says the leading surgeons were booked for consultations six to seven months ahead, and the original poster says two community face raters had named negative canthal tilt and upper eyelid exposure as his main weaknesses. A poster in another thread argues that other eyelid procedures are more established than canthoplasty.[3]

Users also note that "lower eyelid retraction surgery" is a broad label covering many variations, citing a retrospective analysis of 21 procedures in 11 patients that combined midface lift, scar release and a thick AlloDerm graft.[4] Other threads compare orbital implants with almond eye surgery, ask whether retraction affects vision, report one-week healing updates and plan operations months ahead.[29][30][31][32]

The term "almond eye" connects to community vocabulary about canthal tilt, hunter eyes and eye-area harmony, and to a wider conversation about hardmaxxing, the community's name for surgical and procedural routes to a better appearance.

A randomized trial in thyroid eye disease compared retractor tenotomy with an antimetabolite against scleral grafting for lower lid retraction, and an earlier randomized trial studied a technique to minimise lower lid retraction with inferior rectus recession.[16][17] Randomized comparisons of spacer materials include dermis versus auricular cartilage in a 2025 trial and autologous auricular cartilage versus bovine and porcine acellular dermal matrix spacer grafts.[7][8] A randomized comparison of inferomedial versus balanced orbital decompression analysed changes in eyelid parameters.[18]

Several registered trials address lower lid retraction, including dermis versus auricular cartilage grafts and acellular dermal matrix versus autologous tarsus.[19][20] A 2016 review of Graves lower eyelid retraction found that controlled studies comparing techniques were lacking.[5] A 2000 review of retraction after cosmetic surgery describes its presentation and management.[10]

Retraction after blepharoplasty is described as challenging and multifactorial, with surgical correction difficult and unpredictable and a frequent negative effect on the patient's mood, which is why preoperative counselling about expectations is stressed.[2] Persistent retraction can produce dry eye, irritation and corneal exposure.[1] Graft contraction over time has been compared between materials.[9]

The EyeRounds tutorial warns that tightening the lower lid in someone with midface hypoplasia can cause the lid to slide under the globe and worsen retraction, which is one reason surgeons assess the cheek support as well as the lid.[25] Complications reported in the wider eyelid-malposition literature include recurrence, asymmetry, and, for posterior lamellar grafts, changes in lid position on downgaze.[23] Community threads discuss revision difficulty and cases that members describe as unsatisfactory.[3][29]

lore.intro: Forum threads on looksmax.org discuss almond eye surgery as a way to change eye shape and canthal tilt, and compare surgeons, costs and outcomes.[3][4][28]

claims.claim: Almond eye surgery gives a more almond, positively tilted eye
claims.believers: Users describe wanting less scleral show and a more almond shape and share before-and-after cases and plans for surgery.[3]
claims.experts: Published work focuses on repairing retraction from thyroid disease, prior surgery or congenital causes, and reports variable aesthetic improvement after standard surgery. A Korean series reports corrected lid position and satisfactory cosmetic results in treated congenital cases.[2][24]

claims.claim: "Lower eyelid retraction surgery" is a broad term for many different operations
claims.believers: A thread cites a retrospective series of 21 procedures in 11 patients combining midface lift, scar release and AlloDerm graft to show how varied the operations are.[4]
claims.experts: Reviews describe a variety of spacer materials and techniques chosen by severity, with few controlled comparisons.[5][25]

claims.claim: The best results require one of a handful of high-demand surgeons
claims.believers: A ranking thread lists leading US surgeons with consultation fees and six-to-seven-month waits.[3]
claims.experts: Reviews describe correction as difficult and unpredictable and emphasise expectations counselling, with outcomes depending on cause and technique.[2]

claims.claim: Canthoplasty alone gives the almond eye look
claims.believers: Forum threads compare canthoplasty, fat grafts, fillers and retraction surgery as routes to the same look.[28]
claims.experts: A plastic surgeon writing on scleral show describes canthoplasty as best viewed as an adjunct to other surgery, and the EyeRounds tutorial uses canthal tightening as the first step only for mild cases.[25][27]

claims.claim: Orbital or rim implants can be an alternative route to the same eye support
claims.believers: Threads ask users to weigh implants against almond eye surgery.[29]
claims.experts: Published commentary describes infraorbital rim support as part of a combined approach for congenital scleral show; controlled comparisons with retraction surgery have not been published.[27]

claims.claim: Lower eyelid retraction affects vision and eye comfort
claims.believers: A thread asks whether retraction affects vision, and members discuss dryness and irritation.[30]
claims.experts: Persistent retraction can cause dry eye, irritation and corneal exposure, and retraction with exposure keratopathy is treated for protection of the cornea.[1][25]

claims.claim: Fillers can serve as a reversible trial of the look
claims.believers: Users discuss fillers and fat grafts for the under-eye area as lower-commitment options.[28]
claims.experts: Hyaluronic acid expansion of the lower lid has been reported as a temporary option.[14][26]
